How it works

For one-on-ones with teammates or your manager, team calls, reviews, and presentations.

  1. Choose a window

    Open CursorCue and choose the app window you want to share.

  2. Share CursorCue

    In Google Meet, Teams or Zoom, share the window named CursorCue Share.

  3. Keep working

    Use the Tools menu or your shortcuts to freeze, hide, resume or drop the shared cursor. Your real mouse keeps moving in the original app.

Change cursor size and keys in Tools → Cursor size & shortcuts, then Apply.

Questions, answered.

How is the shared cursor different?

CursorCue captures your chosen app without its physical cursor, then adds an independent shared cursor. Share the CursorCue Share window instead of the original app.

Does my real mouse still work?

Yes. Freeze and hide affect the shared cursor. Your physical mouse keeps moving and clicking normally in the original app.

Which Windows versions are supported?

CursorCue runs on 64-bit Windows 11 and Windows 10 version 2004 or later. Share one selected application window.

How do I share CursorCue in a meeting?

In Google Meet, Teams or Zoom, choose to share a window and select CursorCue Share. Keep CursorCue and your source window open and unminimized, then continue working in the original app.
